ON F1 F2, at --std 85 and 2023, and in a FUNCTION definition; the complement also holds (an inner MODE declarative beats an outer GLOBAL FILE one, GR4a). ModeIndex has exactly the three consumers the record names, so there is no fourth selection site. What the record misses is the RULE'S SCOPE: GR5 is 'Within a given procedure division', and ISO 14.2.2 SR10 says Format 1 -- the procedure-division format that CARRIES the DECLARATIVES portion (14.2.1) -- 'may be specified in a source element if and only if that source element is a function definition, a function prototype definition, a METHOD DEFINITION, a program definition, or a program prototype definition'. A method definition therefore has a procedure division that may legally hold Format-1 USE statements (14.9.49.3 SR1 puts the USE statement in exactly that declaratives portion), and the compiler rejects EVERY declarative part inside a method unconditionally: StatementBinder.cs:239-242 -> COBOL0899 'DECLARATIVES inside a method (ISO 14.2.1) are recognized but not yet implemented (owning roadmap phase: Phase 3, OO port)'. That is a deferral rejecting legal source, not owner-documented non-support, so the rule is implemented for the program and function procedure divisions and NOT IMPLEMENTED for a method's. Two halves, one verified => PARTIAL. (The record's code-location, editions and empty test-ref are otherwise accurate and should be kept.) || EDITIONS AS ADJUDICATED: 1985/2002/2014/2023 (FORMAT 1).
